summary: Players draft double-sided domino tiles each round based on a value ranking, then place them edge-to-edge into their own personal kingdom, matching terrain types and chasing crown symbols. It's a light, quick, almost meditative spatial puzzle where the only real interaction is competing over which tiles you get to pick, not what happens on anyone's board.
praised: very easy to teach even to kids
satisfying puzzle of shaping a compact kingdom
criticised: low player interaction beyond the draft
can feel too light or repetitive for serious gamers
little to no catch-up mechanism if you fall behind

interaction.detail: Each player builds their own kingdom grid, so boards are private, but every domino is picked from a shared, visible row and turn order is set by prior picks, so taking a tile can deny a rival the exact terrain or crown combo they wanted. There's no direct interaction with an opponent's kingdom itself, just competition over the shared draft.

sources: territory size × crowns for each connected terrain group
Middle Kingdom bonus for keeping the castle centered (variant)
Harmony bonus for a completed 5x5 grid (variant)
scoring.how_you_win: Draft and place dominoes into your own 5x5 kingdom so that same-terrain squares connect into large crowned territories; once all dominoes have been drafted and placed the game ends, and whoever's summed territory scores (squares x crowns) are highest wins, with ties broken by largest territory then most crowns.
